label: EdgeSwitch 10XP
description: EdgeSwitch 10XP (ES-10XP) - 8x 1G RJ45 all 24 V passive PoE out (15 W per port) + 2x 1G SFP. 20 Gbps switching capacity.

poe.note: DERIVED CEILING, not a quoted budget - Ubiquiti prints no total PoE row for this box, only a per-port cap. The two published figures give the headroom: the included adapter is "24V DC, 2.5A" = 60 W, and "Max. power consumption: 8W (Excluding PoE output)", so at most 60 - 8 = 52 W can leave the eight PSE ports. Same derivation as devices/ubiquiti/uisp-r.json and devices/antaira/lmp-1002g-sfp-t.json. Eight ports at the vendor's 15 W per-port maximum would be 120 W, so the adapter, not the port count, is what stops a full fill.

notes: The eight copper ports source 24 V passive PoE, not 802.3af: the tech-spec table (https://techspecs.ui.com/uisp/wired/es-10xp, HTTP 200, 575,764 B, read 2026-11-20) prints "PoE interface: 24V DC passive PoE (Pins 4, 5+; 7, 8-)" and "Max. passive PoE wattage per port: 15W", and the SKU's own description reads "each equipped with a 24V passive PoE output". Until 2026-11-20 the ports said `poeOutClass: "PoE"`, which in this catalogue's vocabulary is 802.3af - a negotiated 48 V standard a 24 V passive port does not speak, and the fault docs/DEVICE_SCHEMA.md names (test/uisp-r-poe.test.js, test/ep-s16-poe.test.js). The class is now `passive`, which is what `devices/ubiquiti/es-16xp.json` in the same line already declares. The `poe` block is derived, not quoted: see its note. The power adapter is the only difference from the ES-10X (2.5 A here, 1 A there), which is why the 10X is a passthrough box and this one is a PSE.
